outputs.exact_statement: If $\Omega$ has a continuous caustic collar, then $\Omega$ is an ellipse. Equivalently, there are $c\in\mathbb R^2$ and a real symmetric positive-definite matrix $Q$ such that $$\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:(x-c)^TQ(x-c)<1\}.$$ Circles are included.
Under the hypotheses of [thm:main](#thm:main), the support function of the table and its boundary are real analytic.

There is a one-sided phase collar filled by invariant continuous graphs $p=g_b(\theta)$, where $b>0$ increases towards the interior and $g_b$ strictly decreases pointwise. The induced increasing lifts $F_b$ have positive translation numbers $\tau(b)$, tending to zero as $b\downarrow0$.*

*For every sufficiently small positive rational number $l/q$, in lowest terms, there is exactly one graph with $\tau(b)=2\pi l/q$, and its lift satisfies $$\label{ana:rational-identity}
F_b^q(\theta)=\theta+2\pi l
\qquad\text{for every }\theta.$$

For the actual table, the normalized action in [ana:normalized-action](#ana:normalized-action) is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the real diagonal, diagonally $2\pi$-periodic, and antisymmetric. It satisfies $$D(X,X+T)=-T^3/24+O(T^5),\qquad
D_1(X,X+T)=T^2/8+O(T^4),$$ locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives. The unique rational graphs and their identities in [lem:rational-periodicity](#lem:rational-periodicity) are available for every sufficiently small positive reduced $l/q$.

There are $s,r_1>0$, with $r_1<s$, and a real-symmetric holomorphic function $U(y,t)$ on $$\{(y,t):|\Im y|<2s,\ |t|<r_1\}$$ such that $U-y$ is $2\pi$-periodic in $y$, $U$ is even in $t$, $U(y,0)=y$, and $$D_1\bigl(U(y,t),U(y+t,t)\bigr)
 +D_2\bigl(U(y-t,t),U(y,t)\bigr)=0
 \label{joint:stationary-equation}$$ for $|\Im y|<s$, $|t|<r_1$. Here real symmetry means $U(\bar y,\bar t)=\overline{U(y,t)}$.*



*Set $$\Theta(y,t)=\phi(U(y,t)),\qquad
 p(y,t)=-\mathcal S_1\bigl(\Theta(y,t),\Theta(y+t,t)\bigr).
 \label{joint:oriented-coordinates}$$ On a possibly smaller product neighborhood, both functions are holomorphic, real-symmetric, and even in $t$. For positive small real $t$, the billiard map sends the line $(\Theta(y,t),p(y,t))$ to the line $(\Theta(y+t,t),p(y+t,t))$. The variables $(y,t^2)$ give analytic coordinates on a full one-sided phase collar. Moreover, $$dp\wedge d\Theta=A(t)\,dy\wedge dt,
 \qquad A(t)=\frac{c}{4}t+O(t^3),
 \label{eq:area-coefficient}$$ where $A$ is holomorphic and real on the real axis. In particular $t^2$ is a nondegenerate analytic first integral on that collar.

The expressions in [joint:normalized-residual]–[joint:coefficient-a] extend holomorphically to $t=0$, with $$E(U)(y,0)=\frac{(U')^2U''}{4},\qquad a(U)(y,0)=\frac{(U')^3}{4}. \label{joint:zero-parameter}$$ If $U$ is even in $t$, so are $E$ and $a$. The mean of $E$ over a real period in $y$ vanishes. For a variation $\delta U=U'v$, $$E_U(U'v)=\partial(a\partial v)+(Ev)'. \label{joint:linearization}$$ At an exact solution at a nonzero real parameter $t_0$, assign an arbitrary parameter jet $\dot U=U'z$. Its total residual jet is $$\dot E=\partial\left(a\partial z+\frac{a}{t_0}\right). \label{joint:parameter-jet}$$ All these identities hold wherever their shifted arguments are defined.

For every fixed integer $m\ge1$, there are real analytic periodic functions $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ such that $$U^{(m)}(y,t)=y+\sum_{j=1}^m u_j(y)t^{2j}$$ satisfies $E(U^{(m)})=O(t^{2m+2})$. All coefficients are holomorphic on a common fixed smaller y-strip. For $d_0$ sufficiently small, $U^{(m)}$ satisfies the fixed smallness conditions with slack and $\|E(U^{(m)})\|\le C_m d_0^{2m+2}$ on its initial shifted domain.

After the parameter disk has been reduced if necessary, $$h_L(t)=h_X(t)+\frac{|\Im t|}{2}.
 \label{cont:width-equality}$$

Let $(a,\delta)$ range over a small real rectangle $I\times(0,\delta_*)$. Suppose that $\psi_i,w_i$, $1\le i\le m$, and $B$ are analytic in a neighborhood of that rectangle, that the $\psi_i$ are real-valued on the real rectangle, that the $w_i$ are nonzero, and that the differentials $\,\mathrm d\psi_i$ have pairwise distinct directions. Suppose formal one-variable germs $f_i$ at one interior basepoint satisfy $$\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(a,\delta)f_i(\psi_i(a,\delta))=B(a,\delta).
 \label{cont:web-equation}$$ Then these germs converge and continue along the rectangle. If, in addition, $$\psi_i(a,\delta)=a+O(\delta),\qquad
 \partial_a\psi_i(a,\delta)=1+O(\delta)$$ analytically up to $\delta=0$, each continued one-variable germ extends to that edge near every smaller interior subinterval of $I$. No boundedness of the coefficients of the induced differential system at $\delta=0$ is required.

Fix an integer $k\ge2$, and put $L_i=L(y+it,t)$. Every intermediate line $L_i$, $0<i<k$, is algebraic over the differential field generated by $L_0,L_k$. For each fixed $k$, finitely many endpoint derivatives suffice. The same assertion holds for translated index intervals. All derivatives of the intermediate fields are algebraic over the corresponding endpoint differential field.

Let $k\ge2$, and put $P_i=X(y+it,t)$, $0\le i\le k$. Every intermediate point and every edge of this chain is algebraic over the differential field generated by $P_0,P_k$ and the analytic coefficient $A(t)$ in $$\,\mathrm dp\wedge\,\mathrm d\Theta=A(t)\,\,\mathrm dy\wedge\,\mathrm dt.$$ For each fixed $k$, finitely many jets suffice. The assertion persists under translation and analytic continuation.

Let $D_w$ be a connected plane disk and $0<\rho<R$. Suppose that $F(w,\zeta)$ is meromorphic on $$D_w\times\{\rho<|\zeta|<R\}.$$ If it extends meromorphically to $D_0\times\{|\zeta|<R\}$ for some nonempty open subdisk $D_0\subset D_w$, then it extends meromorphically to the whole product $D_w\times\{|\zeta|<R\}$. There is also a holomorphic version: if the original data and the initial extension are holomorphic, the resulting extension is holomorphic.

Suppose a continuous path in one complex center variable has a neighborhood on which a family of analytic disks is holomorphic in the center and disk variables. Assume that the pulled-back primary data are jointly meromorphic on a common boundary collar of these disks, that these collar germs agree on overlaps, and that a nonempty open set of starting centers has a full-disk extension. The extensions then propagate along the center path. The same statement holds holomorphically. In that case a uniform boundary modulus bound, or a uniform bound on the real or imaginary part of a scalar holomorphic component, is preserved inside each disk.
Both $h_L$ and $h_X$ satisfy superharmonic comparison on $B$. They are positive lower semicontinuous superharmonic functions, with the identically infinite case admitted.

Let $F=L$ or $F=X$, and let $t_0\in B\cap\mathbb R$. If $h_F(t_0)=H_1<\infty$, no joint meromorphic patch of the primary branch passes through any point of $\Im y=H_1$. The corresponding assertion at the lower wall follows by real symmetry.

All zeros and poles of $a$ in $D_H$ are simple. At each such center $p$, the curve has the local symmetry $$\Gamma(2p-s)=\Gamma(s),\qquad a(2p-s)=-a(s).
 \label{shape:center-reflection}$$
If $a$ has a zero or a pole in $D_H$, the boundary is an ellipse.

Unless the boundary is a circle, there is a single-valued holomorphic function $\mathfrak s$ on the joint tube $$\mathcal T=\left\{(y,t):t\text{ is in the parameter disk},\quad -h_X(\bar t)<\Im y[shape:global-composition] is void when $H=\infty$.

Every zero of $f$ in $D_H$ is simple. At each such zero, $f''=0$. Consequently $$q=\frac{f''}{f}
 \label{shape:potential-definition}$$ extends holomorphically throughout $D_H$.

For the normalization [shape:mean-normalization], $$\mathfrak s(y,t)=y+t^2V(y)+O(t^4),$$ where $V$ is holomorphic and periodic on $D_H$, has zero mean, and satisfies $$V'=\frac{f^2+8q-\langle f^2+8q\rangle}{120}. \label{eq:V-coefficient}$$

Fix a compact path of frozen states from the small-field germ to a finite point of one of the two displayed actions above, avoiding kernel and root degeneracies, with $J\ne0$ and $p_{JJ}\ne0$ at its endpoint. Suppose analytic fast fields satisfying $F''=QF$ converge locally uniformly to those frozen states on complex neighborhoods of the path and of all its swept integration segments. Continue their glancing square-root germs along the corresponding perturbed path. Their actions then converge analytically, with all derivatives on smaller neighborhoods of the endpoint, to the frozen action on that fixed continued sheet. The endpoint alone does not select a sheet after an arbitrary loop.

Fix $1/2<\alpha<1$, a finite target aperture $m_0$, and a fixed $\delta_b\in(0,H/2)$. There is an input aperture $L$, depending on $\alpha$ and $m_0$, with the following property. Fix $K<\infty$, let $d\to0$, choose real centers $x_0$, and let $0<r\le Kd$. Suppose $$\label{cone:input}
 rM(s)\le\varepsilon(d/\delta_s)^\alpha
 \quad\text{if}\quad
 d/10\le\delta_s\le\delta_b,
 \quad |\Re s-x_0|\le L\delta_s.$$ For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ and then sufficiently small $d$, the lift continues jointly holomorphically along vertical paths from a fixed lower row throughout $$\label{cone:target}
 d<\delta<\delta_*,\qquad
 |\Re y-x_0|<m_0\delta,\qquad
 |t|<r(\delta/d)^\alpha,$$ where $\delta_*>0$ is fixed. With $B=1+(\varepsilon/r)d^\alpha$, it satisfies $$\label{cone:passage-estimate}
 |\mathfrak s(y,t)-y|
 \le C B^2|t|^2\delta^{1-2\alpha}.$$ The relative depth error is small, so these continuations remain in the shape strip, and they agree with the original lift wherever the latter is defined below them.*

*The input aperture can be chosen independently of $K$. Once it contains the fixed geometric enlargements described in the proof, the constant $C$ and the smallness requirement on $\varepsilon$ can be chosen independently of the target aperture. They may depend on $K$, $\alpha$, and the fixed lower-strip data.

The local construction in [thm:cone](#thm:cone) does not use the assertion that $H$ is a singularity height. It remains valid with a reference height $h$ in place of $H$, provided the stated cone and its thickenings are contained in the actual shape domain, lower-row initial data are available, and the relative-error bound keeps the constructed lift in that domain. In a rescaled sequence this formulation is applied on fixed compact sets, with thresholds allowed to depend on the chosen finite aperture. The constants in the estimate remain independent of that aperture. A statement about the global width still uses the actual first boundary of the phase domain, as explained next.
At a finite shape edge, a uniform bound $\max_{\Im s=H-\delta}M(s)=O(\delta^{-p_0})$ with $p_0<1$ is impossible in the nonisotropic alternative.

Suppose, for all sufficiently small $\delta_s$, that $$\delta_s\max_{\Im s=H-\delta_s}M(s)
 \le C\bigl(1+\log(1/\delta_s)\bigr)^A$$ for some fixed $C,A$. Then there are constants $L,C_1,C_2,c_*>0$ such that for every sufficiently large $k=\log(1/d)$ and every real center $x_0$, there is a point $s$ with $$\label{cone:witness-window}
 |\Re s-x_0|\le L\delta_s,\qquad
 k-C_1\log k\le\log(1/\delta_s)\le k+C_2,
 \qquad \delta_sM(s)\ge c_*.$$

Suppose $H<\infty$, and define $$g(k)=\log\max_{\Im s=H-e^{-k}}M(s).$$ In the nonisotropic alternative it is impossible that $$\label{cone:finite-order-assumption}
 1<\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{g(k)}{k}<\infty.$$

There is no sequence of centers $s_n=x_n+\mathrm ih_n\in D_H$, length scales $\ell_n>0$, and field scales $m_n>0$ with the following properties. Put $b_n=\ell_nm_n$ and $$\label{profile:scales} F_n(S)=\frac{f(s_n+\ell_n S)}{m_n},\qquad Q_n(S)=\frac{q(s_n+\ell_n S)}{m_n^2},\qquad Y=\frac{y-s_n}{\ell_n},\quad T=m_nt.$$ Assume that $b_n\to\infty$, that $(D_H-s_n)/\ell_n$ exhausts $\mathbb C$, and that, locally uniformly on $\mathbb C$, either $$\label{profile:exponential-pairs} (F_n,Q_n)\longrightarrow(c_0e^{-\mathrm iS},0) \quad\hbox{or}\quad (F_n,Q_n)\longrightarrow(0,c_0^2e^{-2\mathrm iS}), \qquad c_0\ne0.$$ The following additional assumptions are imposed according to the value of $H$.* 1. *If $H<\infty$, then $h_n\to H$, $\ell_n\to0$, and there are $\alpha_0\in(1/2,1)$ and $\delta_b\in(0,H/2)$ such that, for every fixed $L<\infty$, there is a constant $C_L$ for which eventually $$\label{profile:coarser-cone} M(s)\le C_Lm_n\left(\frac{\ell_n}{\delta}\right)^{\alpha_0}, \qquad \ell_n\le\delta=h_n-\Im s\le\delta_b, \quad |\Re s-x_n|\le L\delta.$$ The exponent is independent of $L$; the constant and the eventual sequence threshold may depend on $L$.* 2. *If $H=\infty$, then $h_n\to\infty$, $0<\ell_n\le C$, and [profile:coarser-cone] holds with a single constant for all horizontal positions and for $\ell_n\le\delta\le h_n$. Moreover, $$\label{profile:entire-log-condition} \log(1+h_n/\ell_n)=o(\log m_n).$$

The model of [profile:energy-model](#profile:energy-model), expressed in the variable $w=Tc_0e^{-\mathrm iY}$, is analytic for $|w|<R$, for some $R>0$. It continues through the boundary circle except possibly at $w=R,-R$. A sufficiently small continuation loop around $w=R$, attached to the inner model, changes the value of $S_*-Y$. The loop and its two adjoining regular corridors can be chosen so that all chord kernels and the twist $p_{JJ}$ remain nonzero, including on the changed branch.

Let a compact corridor of a continued branch of the model in [profile:branch-model](#profile:branch-model) have nonzero kernels and twist, and let $T$ range over a compact set avoiding zero. Suppose two neighboring lift entries are initialized in a joint patch where they converge to that model, with convergence of their first divided difference. Along segments of bounded length made of increments $a_n=T/b_n$, the normalized chord recurrence continues these entries holomorphically and tracks the model with error $o(1)$. The same holds for increments $-T/b_n$. The statement is uniform on compact thickenings of such segments and their initial patches.

In the nonisotropic case, $H=\infty$ implies that the table is a circle. If $H<\infty$, then $$\limsup_{k\to\infty}
 \frac{\log\max_x M(x+\mathrm i(H-e^{-k}))}{k}<\infty.$$

On an inner tile, with a fixed enlargement on the right, $$\label{critical:eq:disk-bound}
 (d_kM)^2\le C\left(1+\sup d_k^2|W|\right).$$

Assume that no sequence in [def:prohibited-sequence](#def:prohibited-sequence) exists. Then there are $C>0$ and $\varepsilon_1\in(0,1)$ such that $$\label{critical:eq:mu-f-saving}
 \mu_f(k)\le C(1+k)^{1-\varepsilon_1}\qquad(k\ge k_0).$$

Assume that no sequence in [def:prohibited-sequence](#def:prohibited-sequence) exists. Then, for all $k\ge k_0$, $$\label{critical:eq:polynomial-bounds}
 \mu(k)\le C(1+k),\qquad
 d_k\max_x M\le C(1+k)^2,\qquad
 d_k\max_x|P|\le C(1+k)^4.$$ All fixed tile enlargements have the corresponding bounds.
There is no sequence satisfying [def:prohibited-sequence](#def:prohibited-sequence).
Alternative (i) of [lem:contact-dichotomy](#lem:contact-dichotomy) is impossible for the moment law of a prohibited sequence.

Let $\Gamma$ be a piecewise smooth Jordan curve, and let $U$ be a connected open neighborhood of a compact path in a complex variable $w$. Suppose $A(T,w)$ is holomorphic on a neighborhood of $\Gamma\times U$. If, for $w$ in some nonempty open subset of $U$, it extends holomorphically to the interior of $\Gamma$, then it has such an extension for every $w\in U$, jointly holomorphic in $T,w$. The extension agrees with the original collar germs.

Fix $$\frac12<c_1<1-\beta,\qquad
 P_1>\max(\lambda,1+a).$$ There is an unbounded set $E\subset(0,\infty)$, with $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(v,E)=o(v)$ as $v\to\infty$, such that every $u\in E$ satisfies, for all real $v$, $$\label{model:epoch-envelope}
 L(v)-L(u)\le
 \begin{cases}
  c_1(v-u),&v\le u,\\
  P_1(v-u),&v\ge u.
 \end{cases}$$

There is a fixed sufficiently large aperture $L_0$ with the following property. For every compact interval $I\subset\mathbb R$, there is an error function $\eta_I(u)\to0$, for $u\in E$, such that every sufficiently large $u\in E$ and every $x\in I$ admit a point $w=p-\mathrm i\delta\in\mathbb H_-$ satisfying $$\label{model:witness-estimate}
 |p-x|\le L_0\delta,\qquad
 |-\log\delta-u|\le\eta_I(u)u,\qquad
 \log|F(w)|\ge\lambda u-\eta_I(u)u.$$ The epochs are common to all centers; a center-dependent subsequence is not needed.

Let $F\not\equiv0$ be holomorphic in $\mathbb H_-:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\Im z<0\}$, and suppose that $F''/F$ extends holomorphically to $\mathbb H_-$. There cannot exist a number $\lambda\ge1$ and an unbounded set of epochs $E\subset(0,\infty)$ with all of the following properties.* 1. *For every compact interval $I\subset\mathbb R$, $$\sup_{x\in I}\log|F(x-\mathrm ie^{-v})| \le \lambda v+o(v),\qquad v\longrightarrow\infty. \label{model:mesh-upper}$$ The error is uniform in $x\in I$.* 2. *The epochs are relatively dense in the sense that $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(v,E)=o(v),\qquad v\longrightarrow\infty. \label{model:mesh-epochs}$$* 3. *For every compact interval $I$, there are a fixed aperture $A_I<\infty$ and a function $r_I(u)\to0$ such that, for every sufficiently large $u\in E$ and every $x\in I$, there is a point $w=p-\mathrm i\delta$ satisfying $$|p-x|\le A_I\delta,\qquad |{-\log\delta}-u|\le r_I(u)u,\qquad \log|F(w)|\ge\lambda u-r_I(u)u. \label{model:mesh-witness}$$* *In particular, the epochs in (iii) are common to all the centers in $I$; no choice of an epoch depending on the center is allowed.

Fix constants $1\le a\le b$ and $K>0$. Let $w=p-\mathrm id$, and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite family of squares $T$ of sides $\rho_T$ and center depths $d_T$, with $$a\rho_T\le d_T\le b\rho_T,\qquad
 d_T\le d/2,\qquad |\Re c_T-p|\le Kd.$$ Choose a rectangle $$R=\{z:|\Re z-p|<Md,\quad \tau<-\Im z<2d\},$$ where $M$ is sufficiently large in terms of $a,b,K$, and $0<\tau<\frac14\min_T d_T$. Suppose that $U\ge0$ is superharmonic in a neighborhood of $\overline R$, that $U(w)<\infty$, and that $U\ge H>0$ on the concentric disks $D_T$ of radius $\rho_T/8$. If $I_T$ is the horizontal projection of $T$, then $$\left|\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal T}I_T\right|
 \le C d\,\frac{U(w)}{H}.
 \label{model:mesh-shadow-bound}$$ Here $C$ depends only on the fixed geometric constants.

Let $Q$ be a square of side $\rho$ and center $c$. Suppose that $F$ is holomorphic on $B(c,100\rho)$, and that $$U=M-\log|F|\ge0
 \quad\text{there},\qquad
 \inf_Q U\le T,$$ where $T>0$. There are disks with sum of radii at most $C h\rho$, for any fixed sufficiently small $h>0$, outside which $$U(z)\le C_hT
 \quad\text{on the concentric square }Q^*\text{ of side }9\rho.
 \label{model:mesh-local-high}$$ The constants are absolute except for the indicated dependence on $h$. A finite simple chain of such squares, in which touching neighbors have side ratios in $[1/2,2]$, can consequently be routed through their enlargements by a polygonal path satisfying the same bound with length at most $C\sum_Q\rho_Q$. The endpoints can be chosen in prescribed squares of side comparable to $\rho_Q$ near the first and last tiles and contained in their respective enlargements; the routing constants may depend on these fixed comparability constants.

In the remaining finite-wall critical case, the angle budget of [thm:angle-budget-reduction](#thm:angle-budget-reduction) and the polynomial bounds of [cor:critical-polynomial-bounds](#cor:critical-polynomial-bounds) hold unconditionally. In particular, for some $\epsilon>0$, $$\int_{k_0}^K\mu_f(k)^2\,\,\mathrm dk\le C K^{2-\epsilon}.$$

The following identities hold meromorphically on the slice: $$\mathcal H w=0,\qquad
 2f_js_j'=(M_0w)_j.
 \label{odd:jacobi-angle}$$ On the real collar, $w_j>0$, $\mathcal H$ is negative semidefinite, and each of its proper principal submatrices is negative definite. The matrix $M_0$ is positive definite there.*

*More generally, let $I$ be a proper subset of the sites and let $F\subseteq I^c$. Retain the sites of $I$ with their actual curvature, retain the sites of $F$ with curvature zero, and delete all other sites. The resulting matrix $$B_{I,F}
  =(M_0)_{I\cup F,I\cup F}
    -\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\mathcal V_i\mathbf 1_{\{i\in I\}}\bigr)
 \label{odd:modified-matrix}$$ is invertible on the real collar. In particular its meromorphic determinant is not identically zero. For an empty retained set we use determinant $1$ and inverse norm $0$.

Let $A(t_0)\ne0$ be the signed area coefficient from [eq:area-coefficient](#eq:area-coefficient), in the directed-edge convention used here. Then $$w_j^2=(-1)^{N-1}\frac{A(t_0)}{N}
       \left(\prod_{i=0}^{N-1}\ell_i\right)
       \det\mathcal H_{\widehat j}.
 \label{eq:cofactor}$$ Here $\mathcal H_{\widehat j}$ denotes the principal matrix with site $j$ deleted.

At almost every point of either horizontal boundary of the phase strip $|\Im y|<h$, the functions $s_0,\ldots,s_{N-1}$ have finite nontangential limits, and at least one of these limits lies on $|\Im s|=H$.

Each process $s_j(y_u)$, before phase exit, is a Brownian motion in the shape strip under the scalar time change $$Q_j(u)=\int_0^u|s_j'(y_v)|^2\,\,\mathrm dv,$$ possibly stopped before shape exit. Its initial horizontal law has a density bounded by a fixed constant relative to uniform measure modulo $2\pi$. In particular:*

1.  *The expected occupation of any nonnegative periodic shape observable, integrated against $\,\mathrm dQ_j$, is bounded by a fixed constant times its ordinary shape-strip occupation from a uniform real start. The total shape clocks have bounded expectation. Moreover, $$\mathbb E\int_0^{\tau_L}
           \mathbf 1_{\{k_j(u)\le K\}}|f_j(y_u)s_j'(y_u)|^2\,\,\mathrm du
           \le C(1+K)^{2\rho}
      \label{odd:angle-clock}$$ for large $K$.*

2.  *At the first hit of a deterministic shape-depth row, the subprobability law of the hit is dominated by a fixed constant times the corresponding law for ordinary shape Brownian motion from a uniform real start. In particular that ordinary horizontal law is uniform.*

3.  *After a first hit of shape depth $\delta$, the remaining shape clock before any later phase stop has tail at most $$C\min\left(1,\frac{\delta}{\sqrt T}\right)
      \label{odd:remaining-shape-clock}$$ at clock time $T>0$. This estimate also holds conditionally at that hit whenever it occurs.*

4.  *For a sufficiently large fixed $C$, with probability tending to one through $\tau_L$, $$k_j(u)\ge K_j(u)-C\log L\qquad\text{for every }j.
      \label{odd:retreat}$$

Let $V\ge U\ge1$ be deterministic. For each fixed proper truthful set $I$ and flat set $F\subseteq I^c$, stop at $\tau_L$, at the first failure of $\mathcal G\le U$, or at the first time an $I$-history exceeds $U$, whichever comes first. Except on an event of probability at most $$\frac{C(1+U)}{1+V},
 \label{odd:inverse-failure}$$ the bound $$\|B_{I,F}^{-1}\|\le\exp(CV)
 \label{odd:inverse-bound}$$ holds throughout this stopped interval. The constant is uniform over the finitely many choices of $I,F$. Thus one may secure all these bounds by a finite union, and subsequently choose $I,F$ as functions of the current state before the common geometry cut, whenever their selected history caps hold.
There is a fixed $\sigma<1$ such that $$\mathcal G(u)\le L^\sigma\qquad(0\le u\le\tau_L)$$ with probability tending to one as $L\to\infty$.

For some fixed $C$, with probability tending to one through $\tau_L$, $$n_y(u)\le CL,\qquad
 \int_0^{\tau_L}r_y(u)^{-2}\,\,\mathrm du\le L^C.
 \label{odd:phase-clock-bounds}$$

For every fixed $\sigma>0$, with probability tending to one as $L\to\infty$, $$\mathcal G(u)\le L^\sigma\qquad(0\le u\le\tau_L).
 \label{odd:all-power-geometry}$$ The phase-depth and phase-clock bounds of [odd:phase-clock](#odd:phase-clock) hold simultaneously. All estimates concern the same fixed odd slice.

Let $(X_m)_{0\le m\le M}$ be an integrable real submartingale, and suppose $$V=\sum_{m=0}^{M-1}\mathbb E(X_{m+1}-X_m)^2<\infty.$$ For $0<h<R$, put $$\mathcal C_h=
 \sum_{m=0}^{M-1}\mathbb E\left[
 \mathbf 1_{\{|X_m|\le h\}}
 \min\{(X_{m+1}-X_m)^2,h^2\}\right].$$ There is an absolute constant $C$ such that $$\label{sign:tanaka-bound}
 \mathcal C_h\le
 C h(h+R+\sqrt V)
 +C M h^2\min\left\{1,\frac{V}{(R-h)^2}\right\}.$$

Suppose that, along a sequence $K\to\infty$, some $j\in[0.9K,2.1K]$ satisfies $\mu(j)\ge K^\alpha$. There is a deterministic $k\in[0.8K,2.2K]$ for which $$\label{sign:row-small-exception}
 \frac1{2\pi}\left|\left\{x\in[0,2\pi]:
 \left|\log|f(x+\mathrm i(H-e^{-k}))|\right|
           \le K^{\alpha/2}\right\}\right|\longrightarrow0.$$

Let $z_0=x+\mathrm i(H-d)$, $d<H/4$, and put $$H_b=1+\sup_{B(z_0,d/2)}\delta\sqrt{|q|}.$$ On $B(z_0,d/8)$, the oscillation of $\mathcal A$ is at most $CH_b$. Moreover, the normalized area $L^2$ norm of $\mathcal A-a$ on that disk, and its normalized length $L^2$ norm on the horizontal diameter, are at most $CH_b$. The same estimates hold for fixed smaller disks and for horizontal segments of length comparable to $d$ with fixed interior margins.
Under [sign:low-moments], uniformly for $1.1K\le v\le1.9K$ and $2\le s\le4$, $$\label{sign:increment-L2} \mathbb E|a(v+s)-a(v)|^2\le CK^{2\alpha}.$$
Under [sign:low-moments], the fraction of pairs $(x,k)\in[0,2\pi]\times[1.2K,1.8K]$ for which $$|a(x+\mathrm i(H-e^{-k}))|\le h_0/4$$ tends to zero.

For every sufficiently large $K$, there is a deterministic $k=k(K)\in[0.8K,2.2K]$ such that, on each shape row of depth $e^{-k}$, $$\label{sign:row-test}
 |\log|f||>K^{\alpha/2}$$ outside a set of relative horizontal measure tending to zero as $K\to\infty$.

For the deterministic level in [thm:row-sign](#thm:row-sign), put $$\label{sign:h1-radius}
 h_1=\tfrac12K^{\alpha/2},\qquad
 r_{\mathrm{rob}}=e^{-k-h_1/4}.$$ Outside a set of relative horizontal measure tending to zero on either tested row, each point $z$ has $$|\log|f(\zeta)||\ge h_1
       \qquad (|\zeta-z|\le r_{\mathrm{rob}}),$$ with constant sign on that disk. In the odd-slice Brownian experiment, for each fixed site the probability that its first hit of the tested shape depth occurs at a point without this property tends to zero.

There is a fixed finite menu of exponents $0<\gamma_m<1$ such that for each large $L$, one deterministic choice $K=L^{\gamma_m}$ has the following event of probability greater than $0.9$: every terminal history $K_j(\tau_L)$ is either at most $K^{\alpha/8}$ or at least $3K$. At least one history is in the second class.
The nonisotropic finite critical-wall case is impossible.
